# World

A world on the server (the overworld, the nether, the end, or another the server loads). A handle is its name, so keeping one is fine: if the world is unloaded its methods answer `nil` or `false`. Positions are world space, in blocks.

A handle: call its methods with a colon, `world:method()`.


A `data()` table, `Item.data` and `nf.json` can keep one: it is saved as what identifies it and comes back as a handle.

## The world itself {#the-world-itself}

### `world:name()` {#name}

Its name, as `nf.worlds.get` takes it: `"world"`, `"world_nether"`.

**Returns** `string`

### `world:exists()` {#exists}

Whether the server has it loaded now.

**Returns** `boolean`

### `world:environment()` {#environment}

What kind of world it is, or `nil` once it has gone. A world of a custom dimension type says `"normal"`.

**Returns** `"normal"\|"nether"\|"end"\|nil`

### `world:is_managed()` {#is_managed}

Whether this project may unload it (`world:unload`): it's one the project's scripts created (`nf.worlds.create`, `nf.worlds.copy`) or named in `netherforge.json`'s `managedWorlds`, and it isn't the server's main world. Any script can find, load and use any world; only managed ones can be taken away.

**Returns** `boolean`

### `world:unload(options?)` {#unload}

Unloads the world: players in it are moved out first (to the spawn of `options.move_players_to`, else of the main world), then the server saves it (unless `save` is `false`) and lets it go. With `delete`, its files are deleted too, off the main thread, and the project forgets it. Only a world this project manages can be unloaded (see `world:is_managed`): any other, the server's main world included, is an error, as is a `move_players_to` in this same world. A world it created stays the project's after a restart; find it again with `nf.worlds.load`.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `options` (optional) | [`WorldUnloadOptions`](types.md#worldunloadoptions) |  |

**Returns** `boolean`: Whether it was unloaded: `false` when it had gone already, or the server (another plugin) kept it.

```lua
arena:unload({ save = false, delete = true, move_players_to = nf.worlds.get("lobby") })
```

### `world:location(position, yaw?, pitch?)` {#location}

A `Location` in this world, for the functions that take one (`player:teleport`, `nf.centities.spawn`). Give both `yaw` and `pitch`, or neither for a location with no facing; a `yaw` alone faces level.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Where. |
| `yaw` (optional) | `number` | Which way it faces horizontally, in degrees (0 south, 90 west). |
| `pitch` (optional) | `number` | How far up or down, in degrees (−90 up, 90 down). |

**Returns** [`Location`](location.md)

```lua
player:teleport(nf.worlds.default():location(vec3(0, 80, 0), 180, 0))
```

### `world:spawn_location()` {#spawn_location}

Where players appear in this world when nothing else decides, or `nil` once the world has gone.

**Returns** [`Location`](location.md)`?`

### `world:set_spawn_location(location_or_position)` {#set_spawn_location}

Moves the world's spawn. A `Location` in another world is an error.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `location_or_position` | [`Location`](location.md)`\|`[`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Where: a `Location` in this world (its facing is used, when it has one) or a position. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when the world has gone.

### `world:min_height()` {#min_height}

The lowest block y there can be, or `nil` once the world has gone.

**Returns** `integer?`

### `world:max_height()` {#max_height}

One above the highest block y there can be, or `nil` once the world has gone.

**Returns** `integer?`

## Time, weather and sky {#time-weather-and-sky}

### `world:time_of_day()` {#time_of_day}

The time of day in ticks, 0 to 23999: 0 is sunrise, 6000 noon, 12000 sunset, 18000 midnight. `nil` once the world has gone. It's the game's clock, not the wall clock (`nf.server.unix_time()`).

**Returns** `integer?`

### `world:set_time_of_day(ticks)` {#set_time_of_day}

Sets the time of day, keeping the day count. Taken modulo 24000. Doesn't stop the clock (that's the daylight cycle game rule).

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ticks` | `integer` | 0 sunrise, 6000 noon, 12000 sunset, 18000 midnight. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when the world has gone.

### `world:is_day()` {#is_day}

Whether it is day here: the time of day is 23000 to 12999, the rest of `is_night`'s. `false` once the world has gone.

**Returns** `boolean`

### `world:is_night()` {#is_night}

Whether it is night here: the time of day is 13000 to 22999, from dusk to just before sunrise, as `/time set night` and a centity's `"night"` spawn time mean it. `false` once the world has gone.

**Returns** `boolean`

### `world:day_count()` {#day_count}

How many whole days have gone by in this world, or `nil` once it has gone.

**Returns** `integer?`

### `world:moon_phase()` {#moon_phase}

Tonight's moon, or `nil` once the world has gone. It moves on a phase each day: full, waning gibbous, last quarter, waning crescent, new, waxing crescent, first quarter, waxing gibbous, then full again.

**Returns** `"full_moon"\|"waning_gibbous"\|"last_quarter"\|"waning_crescent"\|"new_moon"\|"waxing_crescent"\|"first_quarter"\|"waxing_gibbous"\|nil`

```lua
if world:moon_phase() == "full_moon" then
  nf.server.broadcast("<red>The moon is full tonight.")
end
```

### `world:weather()` {#weather}

The weather now, or `nil` once the world has gone. Thunder always comes with rain.

**Returns** `"clear"\|"rain"\|"thunder"\|nil`

### `world:set_weather(weather, options?)` {#set_weather}

Changes the weather, for `options.ticks` or for as long as the game would have kept it. A `ticks` below 1 is an error, as is a key `options` doesn't take.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `weather` | `"clear"\|"rain"\|"thunder"` |  |
| `options` (optional) | [`WeatherOptions`](types.md#weatheroptions) |  |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when the world has gone.

```lua
world:set_weather("thunder", { ticks = 20 * 60 })
```

### `world:sky()` {#sky}

The sky set over the world (`world:set_sky`), as the calling script names it, or `nil` for none (or once the world has gone). A player's own (`player:set_sky`) is theirs alone.

**Returns** `string?`

### `world:set_sky(sky, options?)` {#set_sky}

Sets a sky of the project's over the world (`skies/<id>.json`): everyone in it sees its colours in place of the biomes' own, the sky, fog, clouds and water, fading over `options.fade_ticks`, until it's cleared or another is set. Only what players are shown changes: the world, its biomes, its mobs and its weather are as they were, and a restart clears it. A player's own sky (`player:set_sky`) is shown them instead. A sky the project has no file for is an error, and so is one added since the server started (its colours are biomes, which the game learns as it starts: restart the server).

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sky` | `string` | A sky of the project's (its file's name under `skies/`, or `namespace:id` for one a package it depends on exports). |
| `options` (optional) | [`SkyOptions`](types.md#skyoptions) |  |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when the world has gone.

```lua
world:set_sky("blood_moon", { fade_ticks = 100 })
```

### `world:clear_sky(options?)` {#clear_sky}

Takes the world's sky away (`world:set_sky`): its biomes' own colours come back over `options.fade_ticks`. Nothing when it has none.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `options` (optional) | [`SkyOptions`](types.md#skyoptions) |  |

```lua
world:clear_sky({ fade_ticks = 100 })
```

## Blocks {#blocks-section}

### `world:block(position)` {#block}

The block at a position: a handle that reads the world live, so it sees later changes. The position is floored to the block it's in. `nil` once the world has gone.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Any point in the block. |

**Returns** [`Block`](block.md)`?`

```lua
local below = this:world():block(this:position() - vec3(0, 1, 0))
```

### `world:blocks(from, to, options?)` {#blocks}

Every block in a box, read in one call: for code that needs many blocks at once (a mob's collision, a flood fill of a room), where a `world:block` and a `:kind()` per block would cost each one. The corners are floored to the blocks they're in and both are included, in any order. What each block is given as is `options.what`. At most 32,768 blocks (32 × 32 × 32): a bigger box is an error. `nil` when any of the box is in a chunk that isn't loaded, or the world has gone.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | One corner: any point in its block. |
| `to` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | The opposite corner, included: any point in its block. |
| `options` (optional) | [`BlockBoxOptions`](types.md#blockboxoptions) |  |

**Returns** [`BlockBox`](types.md#blockbox)`?`

```lua
local box = world:blocks(vec3(0, 60, 0), vec3(15, 70, 15), { what = "class" })
if box then
  -- A block within the box, counted from its corner.
  local function at(x, y, z)
    return box.cells[1 + x + box.size_x * (z + box.size_z * y)]
  end
  if at(0, 0, 0) == 2 then log("solid") end
end
```

### `world:set_block(position, state, options?)` {#set_block}

Changes the block at a position. A block state the server doesn't have (an unknown block, property or value) is an error. Blocks in chunks that aren't loaded can't be read or changed: that answers `nil` or `false`, and never loads the chunk (`world:load_chunk` does).

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Any point in the block. |
| `state` | `string` | A block state: `"minecraft:stone"`, `"minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east]"`. Properties left out take their defaults. |
| `options` (optional) | [`BlockSetOptions`](types.md#blocksetoptions) |  |

**Returns** `boolean`: Whether it changed: `false` in an unloaded chunk or a world that's gone.

```lua
world:set_block(vec3(10, 64, 10), "minecraft:gold_block")
```

### `world:fill_blocks(from, to, state, options?)` {#fill_blocks}

Sets every block in the box between two corners (both included) to one state. One call changes at most 32768 blocks: a bigger box is an error (`fill_gradually` spreads a big fill over several ticks). A block state the server doesn't have is an error. Blocks in unloaded chunks are skipped.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | One corner. |
| `to` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | The opposite corner. |
| `state` | `string` | A block state, as `set_block` takes it. |
| `options` (optional) | [`BlockSetOptions`](types.md#blocksetoptions) |  |

**Returns** `integer`: How many blocks it changed: 0 in a world that has gone.

```lua
nf.task(function()
  for y = 64, 127 do
    world:fill_blocks(vec3(0, y, 0), vec3(63, y, 63), "minecraft:air")
    nf.wait(1)
  end
end)
```

### `world:fill_gradually(from, to, state, options?, callback?)` {#fill_gradually}

Sets every block in the box between two corners (both included) to one state, like `fill_blocks`, but over as many ticks as it takes, for a box too big for one call: up to 16777216 blocks (256 × 256 × 256). It goes a few thousand blocks a tick, shared with every other gradual placement and fill on the server (the owner's `structures.blocks-per-tick` in `config.yml`), so even a big one never stalls the server; each package may have a few going at once (`structures.max-jobs-per-package`), past which one fails at once. It goes a chunk's column at a time, from the bottom up, loading the chunks the box covers as it reaches them (`fill_blocks` skips unloaded ones). A bigger box, a block state the server doesn't have, or a `per_tick` below 1 is an error at once. The world going, or this script stopping, stops it part way, and what was set stays. It takes as many ticks as the fill does, so its changed arrives later: give `callback`, which is called with `changed, err` once it's done, or call it inside a task (`nf.task`) without one, and it waits and returns `changed, err`. Without a callback outside a task, it's an error. When it fails, `changed` is `nil` and `err` says why.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | One corner. |
| `to` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | The opposite corner. |
| `state` | `string` | A block state, as `set_block` takes it. |
| `options` (optional) | [`GradualFillOptions`](types.md#gradualfilloptions) |  |
| `callback` (optional) | `fun(changed: integer?, err: string?)` | Called on the main thread once it's done, as this script's code, with how many blocks it changed (a block that was already that state is not counted) (or `nil` and why not). Not called if the script has stopped by then. |

**Returns** `integer?`: Only without a callback, in a task: how many blocks it changed (a block that was already that state is not counted), or `nil`., `string?`: Why it failed, when it did; `nil` when it worked.

```lua
world:fill_gradually(vec3(-200, 0, -200), vec3(199, 120, 199), "minecraft:air", nil, function(changed, err)
  if err then
    print("The clear-out stopped: " .. err)
  else
    nf.server.broadcast(changed .. " blocks cleared")
  end
end)
```

### `world:flood(start, options)` {#flood}

Fills outward from a block through every block `options.through` names, one neighbour at a time, as far as it reaches: the blocks of a tree (`through = { "#minecraft:logs" }`), the air of a room (`through = { "passable" }`), a lake. It answers every block it filled (`positions`, nearest first by steps) and every block it stopped at (`edges`: a room's walls), with what each is when asked (`kinds`), and `stopped` says why it didn't finish when it didn't: it hit its `limit`, a chunk that isn't loaded or the world's top or bottom (`"unloaded"`: a room open to the sky or the unknown), or its `bounds`. It runs in the server, reading the blocks a box at a time, so a fill of thousands of blocks costs a script one call. A start block it can't fill through answers no positions, and the start as an edge. Blocks in chunks that aren't loaded can't be read or changed: that answers `nil` or `false`, and never loads the chunk (`world:load_chunk` does).

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `start` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Any point in the block to start from. |
| `options` | [`FloodOptions`](types.md#floodoptions) |  |

**Returns** [`FloodResult`](types.md#floodresult)`?`: `nil` once the world has gone.

```lua
local room = world:flood(assert(player:position()), { through = { "passable" }, except = { "#minecraft:doors" }, limit = 750, kinds = true })
if room and not room.stopped then
  log(#room.positions .. " blocks of air, walled in by " .. #room.edges)
end
```

### `world:highest_block(position)` {#highest_block}

The highest block at a column that isn't air, ignoring the position's `y`. `nil` in an unloaded chunk, or a world that has gone.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Any point in the column. |

**Returns** [`Block`](block.md)`?`

## Chunks and biomes {#chunks-and-biomes}

### `world:is_chunk_loaded(position)` {#is_chunk_loaded}

Whether the chunk a position is in is loaded: whether its blocks can be read and changed now.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Any point in the chunk. |

**Returns** `boolean`

### `world:load_chunk(position)` {#load_chunk}

Loads the chunk a position is in, now, generating it if it's new: that can take a while, so do it rarely. The server unloads it again when nobody is near, as it does any chunk.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Any point in the chunk. |

**Returns** `boolean`: Whether it's loaded: `false` for a world that has gone.

### `world:locate_biome(id, options?, callback?)` {#locate_biome}

Finds the nearest place where the world's generator puts a biome, as `/locate biome` does: it asks the generator, so it finds places in chunks nobody has been to, and never loads or generates a chunk. It looks out from `options.near` in a square spiral, every 32 blocks across and 64 up and down, so the place it gives is in the biome but may be up to 32 blocks past its nearest edge, and a biome narrower than that can be missed. A biome the world's generator never places (a nether biome in the overworld) is found nowhere at once. An id that isn't a biome on this server (a bare id that isn't one of the project's is an error saying how to write the game's), or a `radius` out of range, is an error at once. Finding nothing within the radius, or a world that has gone, fails. It works off the main thread, so its position arrives later: give `callback`, which is called with `position, err` once it's done, or call it inside a task (`nf.task`) without one, and it waits and returns `position, err`. Without a callback outside a task, it's an error. When it fails, `position` is `nil` and `err` says why.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | The biome, named as a file names one: the project's own by its id (`"ruby_grove"`, `biomes/ruby_grove.json`), a package's `"acme:grove"` (if it exports it), the game's always written in full (`"minecraft:desert"`). |
| `options` (optional) | [`BiomeSearchOptions`](types.md#biomesearchoptions) |  |
| `callback` (optional) | `fun(position: `[`Vec3`](vec3.md)`?, err: string?)` | Called on the main thread once it's done, as this script's code, with the place it found: a block position in this world, at the height it found the biome (or `nil` and why not). Not called if the script has stopped by then. |

**Returns** [`Vec3`](vec3.md)`?`: Only without a callback, in a task: the place it found: a block position in this world, at the height it found the biome, or `nil`., `string?`: Why it failed, when it did; `nil` when it worked.

```lua
nf.task(function()
  local desert, err = world:locate_biome("minecraft:desert", { near = player:position() })
  if not desert then
    player:send_message("No desert near: " .. err)
    return
  end
  local ground = world:highest_block(desert)
  if ground then
    player:teleport(world:location(ground:position() + vec3(0.5, 1, 0.5)))
  end
end)
```

## Entities {#entities-section}

### `world:players()` {#players}

Everyone in this world now. Empty once the world has gone.

**Returns** [`Player`](player.md)`[]`

### `world:centities(filter?)` {#centities}

The live centity instances in this world: the same as `nf.centities.all` with this world as the filter's `world`.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `filter` (optional) | [`CentityFilter`](types.md#centityfilter) | Only some of them, as `nf.centities.all` takes it. Its `world`, if given, must be this one. |

**Returns** [`Centity`](centity.md)`[]`

### `world:entities(filter?)` {#entities}

The entities in this world's loaded chunks, players included (as `Player` handles), or those the filter picks. Never the entities centities are drawn with. Empty once the world has gone. A filter key that isn't one of `EntityFilter`'s is an error.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `filter` (optional) | [`EntityFilter`](types.md#entityfilter) | Only one kind, one tag, living ones, or those near a point. |

**Returns** [`Entity`](entity.md)`[]`

```lua
for _, zombie in ipairs(world:entities({ kind = "minecraft:zombie", near = here, radius = 16 })) do
  zombie:set_glowing(true)
end
```

### `world:spawn_entity(kind, location_or_position, options?)` {#spawn_entity}

Spawns an entity, set up as `options` say before anything sees it (its `entity_spawn` handlers included). A kind the server doesn't have, or one that can't be spawned (a player), is an error.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `string` | What: `"minecraft:zombie"`. |
| `location_or_position` | [`Location`](location.md)`\|`[`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Where: a `Location` in this world (facing its way, when it has a facing), or a position. |
| `options` (optional) | [`EntitySpawnOptions`](types.md#entityspawnoptions) |  |

**Returns** [`Entity`](entity.md)`?`: The new entity, or `nil` when the world has gone, its chunk isn't loaded, or an `entity_spawn` handler (or another plugin) cancelled it.

```lua
local guard = world:spawn_entity("minecraft:iron_golem", vec3(0, 64, 0), {
  custom_name = "<aqua>Guard",
  tags = { "guard" },
  data = { post = vec3(0, 64, 0) },
})
```

### `world:spawn_item(position, item)` {#spawn_item}

Drops an item stack at a position, as if a block broke there. An item table with a misspelled field, or an item the server doesn't have, is an error.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Where, in this world. |
| `item` | [`Item`](types.md#item) |  |

**Returns** [`DroppedItem`](droppeditem.md)`?`: The dropped item, or `nil` when the world has gone, its chunk isn't loaded, or something cancelled it.

## Particles, sounds and explosions {#particles-sounds-and-explosions}

### `world:spawn_particle(particle, position, options?)` {#spawn_particle}

Spawns particles at a position. The particle's id comes from the server (`"minecraft:flame"`), and which options it takes depends on its kind: `color` and `size` for dust, `color` for coloured particles, `block_state` for block particles, `item` for item particles. An unknown particle, an option it doesn't take, or one it needs left out is an error. Particles that need data NetherForge can't send (vibrations, trails) are an error too. Players see them within 32 blocks, or 128 with `force`.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `particle` | `string` | A particle id: `"minecraft:flame"`, `"minecraft:dust"`. |
| `position` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Where, in the world. |
| `options` (optional) | [`ParticleOptions`](types.md#particleoptions) |  |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when the world has gone.

```lua
world:spawn_particle("minecraft:dust", this:position() + vec3(0, 1, 0), {
  count = 20, spread = vec3(0.3, 0.3, 0.3), color = "#ff8800", size = 1.5,
})
```

### `world:play_sound(sound, position, options?)` {#play_sound}

Plays a sound at a position, for everyone near enough to hear it. A Minecraft sound (`"minecraft:block.note_block.pling"`, checked against the server's sounds) or a resource pack sound (`"<pack>/<key>"`, like `"ui/click"`, your package's own, or another loaded package's as `"<namespace>:<pack>/<key>"`: [looks are values](packages.md#looks-are-values)). An unknown sound is an error.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sound` | `string` | A sound id. |
| `position` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Where it comes from, in the world. |
| `options` (optional) | [`SoundOptions`](types.md#soundoptions) |  |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when the world has gone.

```lua
world:play_sound("minecraft:block.note_block.pling", block:position(), { pitch = 1.5 })
```

### `world:explode(position, power, options?)` {#explode}

Makes an explosion at a position, as TNT would (TNT's power is 4): it damages and knocks back entities, and breaks blocks unless `break_blocks` is `false`.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Its centre. |
| `power` | `number` | How strong: 4 is TNT, 6 a charged creeper. At least 0. |
| `options` (optional) | [`ExplosionOptions`](types.md#explosionoptions) |  |

**Returns** `boolean`: Whether it went off: `false` when another plugin stopped it, or the world has gone.

### `world:strike_lightning(position, options?)` {#strike_lightning}

Strikes lightning at a position: it sets fire and hurts what it hits, unless `effect_only`.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Where it lands. |
| `options` (optional) | [`LightningOptions`](types.md#lightningoptions) |  |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when the world has gone.

## Raycasts and overlaps {#raycasts-and-overlaps}

### `world:raycast(from, direction, max_distance, options?)` {#raycast}

Casts a ray from a point and answers the first thing it hits within `max_distance`: a block's collision shape, an entity's hitbox, or a centity's hitbox (tested with the same shapes clicks are). `nil` when it hits nothing, and in a world that has gone. Blocks in unloaded chunks aren't hit.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Where the ray starts, in the world. |
| `direction` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Which way it goes: any length but zero. |
| `max_distance` | `number` | How far it reaches, in blocks. |
| `options` (optional) | [`RaycastOptions`](types.md#raycastoptions) |  |

**Returns** [`RaycastHit`](types.md#raycasthit)`?`

```lua
local world, eyes, facing = player:world(), player:eye_position(), player:direction()
local hit = world and eyes and facing and world:raycast(eyes, facing, 20)
if hit and hit.centity then
  hit.centity:play_animation("wobble")
end
```

### `world:sweep(from, to, options?)` {#sweep}

Moves a sphere of `options.radius` (0, a point, by default) from one point to another and answers everything it touches on the way, in the order it meets them: what a fast or piercing shot passes through in a tick, which a ray (stopping at the first thing) can't say. Blocks stop it unless `blocks = false`: the block it meets is then the last hit, with its `normal`, and nothing past it is found. It finds centities by their hitboxes (each shown node's boxes, as `raycast` and physics see them; a hidden node has none), players and other entities by theirs, as `options` allows: everything, by default. A centity is found once, by its nearest node. Only what's in loaded chunks is found. An empty list (or `nil`) in a world that has gone.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Where it starts, in the world. |
| `to` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Where it would end. |
| `options` (optional) | [`SweepOptions`](types.md#sweepoptions) |  |

**Returns** [`QueryHit`](types.md#queryhit)`[]`

```lua
local position, velocity = vec3(0, 65, 0), vec3(2, 0, 0)
local hits = world:sweep(position, position + velocity, { radius = 0.25, players = false })
for _, hit in ipairs(hits) do
  if hit.block then
    break -- it struck a wall
  elseif hit.centity then
    hit.centity:emit("game:hit", { damage = 5 })
  end
end
```

### `world:overlap_box(min, max, options?)` {#overlap_box}

Everything whose hitbox is inside or touches a box, nearest the box's middle first. It finds centities by their hitboxes (each shown node's boxes, as `raycast` and physics see them; a hidden node has none), players and other entities by theirs, as `options` allows: everything, by default. A centity is found once, by its nearest node. Only what's in loaded chunks is found. An empty list (or `nil`) in a world that has gone.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `min` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | One corner, in the world. |
| `max` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | The opposite corner. The corners may come in either order. |
| `options` (optional) | [`QueryOptions`](types.md#queryoptions) |  |

**Returns** [`QueryHit`](types.md#queryhit)`[]`

```lua
local corner = vec3(0, 64, 0)
for _, hit in ipairs(world:overlap_box(corner, corner + vec3(4, 3, 4), { players = false })) do
  if hit.centity then
    hit.centity:remove()
  end
end
```

### `world:overlap_sphere(center, radius, options?)` {#overlap_sphere}

Everything whose hitbox comes within `radius` of a point, nearest first: what an explosion or an aura reaches. It finds centities by their hitboxes (each shown node's boxes, as `raycast` and physics see them; a hidden node has none), players and other entities by theirs, as `options` allows: everything, by default. A centity is found once, by its nearest node. Only what's in loaded chunks is found. An empty list (or `nil`) in a world that has gone.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `center` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | The middle, in the world. |
| `radius` | `number` | In blocks, at least 0. |
| `options` (optional) | [`QueryOptions`](types.md#queryoptions) |  |

**Returns** [`QueryHit`](types.md#queryhit)`[]`

```lua
for _, hit in ipairs(world:overlap_sphere(vec3(0, 64, 0), 4, { entities = false })) do
  log(hit.distance)
end
```

### `world:overlap_cone(origin, direction, length, angle, options?)` {#overlap_cone}

Everything whose hitbox reaches into a cone from a point, nearest first: what a swing or a breath in front of someone reaches. A hitbox counts when its point nearest the cone's axis is within `length` of the tip and within `angle` of the axis, or the tip is inside it. It finds centities by their hitboxes (each shown node's boxes, as `raycast` and physics see them; a hidden node has none), players and other entities by theirs, as `options` allows: everything, by default. A centity is found once, by its nearest node. Only what's in loaded chunks is found. An empty list (or `nil`) in a world that has gone.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `origin` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | The cone's tip, in the world. |
| `direction` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Which way it opens: any length but zero. |
| `length` | `number` | How far it reaches from the tip, in blocks, at least 0. |
| `angle` | `number` | How wide it opens, in degrees from its axis to its side: 0 to 180 (90 is everything in front, 180 a sphere). |
| `options` (optional) | [`QueryOptions`](types.md#queryoptions) |  |

**Returns** [`QueryHit`](types.md#queryhit)`[]`

```lua
local eyes, facing = assert(player:eye_position()), assert(player:direction())
for _, hit in ipairs(world:overlap_cone(eyes, facing, 3, 45, { exclude = { player } })) do
  if hit.centity then
    hit.centity:emit("game:struck", { by = player })
  end
end
```

### `world:nearest(position, radius, options?)` {#nearest}

The nearest thing whose hitbox comes within `radius` of a point, or `nil` when there's nothing: what a homing shot or a mob looking for a target wants. With `line_of_sight = true`, only something a ray from the point reaches without a block in the way. It finds centities by their hitboxes (each shown node's boxes, as `raycast` and physics see them; a hidden node has none), players and other entities by theirs, as `options` allows: everything, by default. A centity is found once, by its nearest node. Only what's in loaded chunks is found. An empty list (or `nil`) in a world that has gone.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Where to look from, in the world. |
| `radius` | `number` | How far to look, in blocks, at least 0. |
| `options` (optional) | [`QueryOptions`](types.md#queryoptions) |  |

**Returns** [`QueryHit`](types.md#queryhit)`?`

```lua
local target = world:nearest(assert(this:position()), 16, { centities = false, line_of_sight = true })
if target and target.entity then
  this:look_at(target.position)
end
```

## Game rules and spawning {#game-rules-and-spawning}

### `world:game_rule(rule)` {#game_rule}

A game rule's value: a `boolean` or an `integer`, depending on the rule. `nil` once the world has gone. A rule the server doesn't have is an error.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rule` | `string` | Its id, as the server names it: `"keep_inventory"`, `"random_tick_speed"`. |

**Returns** `any`

### `world:set_game_rule(rule, value)` {#set_game_rule}

Sets a game rule in this world. A rule the server doesn't have, or a value of the wrong type for it (a `boolean` rule given a number), is an error.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rule` | `string` | Its id: `"keep_inventory"`. |
| `value` | `any` | A `boolean` or an `integer`, as the rule takes. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when the world has gone.

```lua
world:set_game_rule("keep_inventory", true)
```

### `world:spawn_limit(category)` {#spawn_limit}

How many mobs of a spawn category the game keeps around each player here before it stops spawning more (the mob cap, per player, scaled by how many chunks are loaded around them), or `nil` once the world has gone. It's this world's own setting, or the server's (`bukkit.yml`) when the world has none.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `category` | `"monster"\|"animal"\|"water_animal"\|"water_ambient"\|"water_underground_creature"\|"ambient"\|"axolotl"` | Which mobs count: `"monster"` for hostile ones, `"animal"` for farm animals, `"ambient"` for bats, and so on. |

**Returns** `integer?`

### `world:set_spawn_limit(category, limit)` {#set_spawn_limit}

Sets this world's mob cap for a spawn category (see `world:spawn_limit`). `0` stops that category spawning naturally. A negative number goes back to the server's own setting. Mobs already there stay.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `category` | `"monster"\|"animal"\|"water_animal"\|"water_ambient"\|"water_underground_creature"\|"ambient"\|"axolotl"` | Which mobs count. |
| `limit` | `integer` | The most of them there may be. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when the world has gone.

```lua
world:set_spawn_limit("monster", 30)
```

### `world:spawn_interval(category)` {#spawn_interval}

How many ticks pass between the game's attempts to spawn mobs of a spawn category here, or `nil` once the world has gone. It's this world's own setting, or the server's (`bukkit.yml`) when the world has none.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `category` | `"monster"\|"animal"\|"water_animal"\|"water_ambient"\|"water_underground_creature"\|"ambient"\|"axolotl"` | Which mobs. |

**Returns** `integer?`

### `world:set_spawn_interval(category, ticks)` {#set_spawn_interval}

Sets how many ticks pass between spawn attempts for a spawn category in this world (see `world:spawn_interval`): lower is faster. `0` stops that category spawning naturally. A negative number goes back to the server's own setting.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `category` | `"monster"\|"animal"\|"water_animal"\|"water_ambient"\|"water_underground_creature"\|"ambient"\|"axolotl"` | Which mobs. |
| `ticks` | `integer` | Ticks between attempts. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when the world has gone.

```lua
world:set_spawn_interval("monster", 2)
```

## Border and structures {#border-and-structures}

### `world:border()` {#border}

The world's border: the wall players can't pass, shown to everyone in the world (except a player given a border of their own with `player:border()`). `nil` once the world has gone.

**Returns** [`WorldBorder`](worldborder.md)`?`

```lua
local border = world:border()
if border then
  border:set_center(vec3(0, 0, 0))
  border:set_size(200)
  border:set_size(20, { ticks = 20 * 60 })
end
```

### `world:save_structure(id, from, to, options?)` {#save_structure}

Saves the box between two corners (both included) as a structure named `id`, to place later with `place_structure`: an arena to reset, a prefab to stamp. It's saved in the server's data folder, not the project, and kept across restarts; saving the same id again replaces it. An id that isn't an id (lowercase letters, digits and `_`), or that one of the project's structures (`structures/<id>.nbt`) or builds (`builds/<id>/`) already has, is an error, as is a box over 48 blocks along any side. Air is saved too, so placing it puts back the empty space as well; it loads the chunks the box covers, as `/place` does.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | Its name: `"arena_reset"`. |
| `from` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | One corner. |
| `to` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | The opposite corner. |
| `options` (optional) | [`StructureSaveOptions`](types.md#structuresaveoptions) |  |

**Returns** `boolean`: Whether it was saved: `false` when the world has gone, or the file couldn't be written.

```lua
world:save_structure("arena_reset", vec3(0, 60, 0), vec3(47, 90, 47), { entities = false })
```

### `world:place_structure(id, position, options?)` {#place_structure}

Places a structure with its smallest corner at `position` (before it's turned): one of the project's (`structures/<id>.nbt`) or one a script saved (`save_structure`). Loads the chunks it covers, as `/place` does, all in this tick: `place_gradually` spreads a big one over several. A build (`builds/<id>/`) is always placed that way, so naming one here is an error, as is a structure there's none of, one whose file can't be read, a `rotation` that isn't a multiple of 90 or an `integrity` outside 0 to 1.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | Which structure. |
| `position` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Where its smallest corner goes, floored to a block. |
| `options` (optional) | [`StructurePlaceOptions`](types.md#structureplaceoptions) |  |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when the world has gone.

```lua
world:place_structure("arena_reset", vec3(0, 60, 0), { rotation = 90, mirror = "none", integrity = 1, entities = false })
```

### `world:place_gradually(id, position, options?, callback?)` {#place_gradually}

Places a structure or a build (`builds/<id>/`, a structure too big for one file) like `place_structure`, its smallest corner at `position` before it's turned, but over as many ticks as it takes. It goes a few thousand blocks a tick, shared with every other gradual placement and fill on the server (the owner's `structures.blocks-per-tick` in `config.yml`), so even a big one never stalls the server; each package may have a few going at once (`structures.max-jobs-per-package`), past which one fails at once. Its blocks go in from the bottom up (a build's a part at a time), loading the chunks it covers as it reaches them, then its entities, once every block is in. Blocks go in as they were saved, with no updates to their neighbours, as `/place` puts them. A structure or build there's none of, a `rotation` that isn't a multiple of 90, an `integrity` outside 0 to 1 or a `per_tick` below 1 is an error at once. A part that can't be read, the world going, or this script stopping stops it part way, and what was placed stays. It takes as many ticks as the placing does, so its placed arrives later: give `callback`, which is called with `placed, err` once it's done, or call it inside a task (`nf.task`) without one, and it waits and returns `placed, err`. Without a callback outside a task, it's an error. When it fails, `placed` is `nil` and `err` says why.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | Which structure or build. |
| `position` | [`Vec3`](vec3.md) | Where its smallest corner goes, floored to a block. |
| `options` (optional) | [`GradualPlaceOptions`](types.md#gradualplaceoptions) |  |
| `callback` (optional) | `fun(placed: integer?, err: string?)` | Called on the main thread once it's done, as this script's code, with how many blocks it placed (those `integrity` left out, or outside the world's heights, are not counted) (or `nil` and why not). Not called if the script has stopped by then. |

**Returns** `integer?`: Only without a callback, in a task: how many blocks it placed (those `integrity` left out, or outside the world's heights, are not counted), or `nil`., `string?`: Why it failed, when it did; `nil` when it worked.

```lua
nf.task(function()
  local placed, err = world:place_gradually("castle", vec3(0, 64, 0), { rotation = 90 })
  if not placed then
    print("The castle stopped part way: " .. err)
    return
  end
  nf.server.broadcast("The castle is up: " .. placed .. " blocks")
end)
```

## Events

What `world:on(event, handler)` listens for. See [Events](events.md) for how events work.

### Blocks

| Event | Payload | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `block_break` | [BlockBreakEvent](types.md#blockbreakevent) | A player is breaking a block in this world: before `nf.on("block_break")`, with the same event, so `event:cancel()` here stops it and `event:stop()` keeps it from `nf`. Assign `event.drops` and `event.experience` to change what it drops. **Cancellable.** Bubbles. Writable: `drops`, `experience`. |
| `block_start_break` | [BlockStartBreakEvent](types.md#blockstartbreakevent) | A player started hitting a block to break it. `event:cancel()` stops them breaking it; assign `event.instant = true` to break it at once, or `false` to make them wait for it. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_start_break")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. **Cancellable.** Bubbles. Writable: `instant`. |
| `block_drop_item` | [BlockDropItemEvent](types.md#blockdropitemevent) | A block a player broke is dropping its items, its contents included (a chest's, a furnace's): after `block_break`, once it has gone. `event:cancel()` drops nothing. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_drop_item")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. **Cancellable.** Bubbles. |
| `block_place` | [BlockPlaceEvent](types.md#blockplaceevent) | A player is placing a block in this world: before `nf.on("block_place")`, with the same event. **Cancellable.** Bubbles. |
| `block_explode` | [ExplodeEvent](types.md#explodeevent) | A block exploded: a bed in the nether or the end, a respawn anchor charged away from the overworld. `event:cancel()` stops the explosion breaking anything; assign `event.breaks_blocks = false` to keep every block standing but still hurt what is near, or `event.yield` to change how much of what breaks drops. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_explode")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. **Cancellable.** Bubbles. Writable: `breaks_blocks`, `yield`. |
| `block_ignite` | [BlockIgniteEvent](types.md#blockigniteevent) | A block is catching fire: flint and steel, a fire charge, lava, lightning, fire spreading, an explosion. `event:cancel()` keeps it from burning. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_ignite")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. **Cancellable.** Bubbles. |
| `block_burn` | [BlockBurnEvent](types.md#blockburnevent) | A block is burning away in a fire. `event:cancel()` keeps it there (it may still catch fire again). In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_burn")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. **Cancellable.** Bubbles. |
| `block_spread` | [BlockChangeEvent](types.md#blockchangeevent) | A block is spreading to another: grass, mycelium, moss, vines, mushrooms, fire, sculk. `event.block` is where it spreads to, `event.source` where from. `event:cancel()` stops it. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_spread")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. **Cancellable.** Bubbles. |
| `block_flow` | [BlockFlowEvent](types.md#blockflowevent) | Water or lava is flowing into another block (or a dragon egg teleporting there). `event:cancel()` stops it. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_flow")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. **Cancellable.** Bubbles. |
| `block_grow` | [BlockChangeEvent](types.md#blockchangeevent) | A crop, sapling stage, sugar cane, cactus, bamboo, pumpkin or melon is growing by itself (bone meal included). `event:cancel()` stops it. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_grow")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. **Cancellable.** Bubbles. |
| `block_fade` | [BlockChangeEvent](types.md#blockchangeevent) | A block is fading by itself: ice or snow melting, coral dying, fire burning out, farmland drying. `event:cancel()` keeps it as it is. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_fade")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. **Cancellable.** Bubbles. |
| `block_form` | [BlockChangeEvent](types.md#blockchangeevent) | A block is forming by itself: snow falling, ice freezing, concrete setting, obsidian or cobblestone from lava, frost walker ice or a snow golem's trail (`event.entity` says which). `event:cancel()` stops it. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_form")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. **Cancellable.** Bubbles. |
| `leaves_decay` | [BlockEvent](types.md#blockevent) | Leaves are decaying, far from any log. `event:cancel()` keeps them. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("leaves_decay")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. **Cancellable.** Bubbles. |
| `piston_extend` | [PistonEvent](types.md#pistonevent) | A piston is pushing out. `event:cancel()` keeps it in, and everything it would push where it is. In this world: heard before `nf.on("piston_extend")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. **Cancellable.** Bubbles. |
| `piston_retract` | [PistonEvent](types.md#pistonevent) | A piston is pulling back. `event:cancel()` keeps it out, and (for a sticky one) the block it would pull where it is. In this world: heard before `nf.on("piston_retract")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. **Cancellable.** Bubbles. |
| `block_redstone` | [BlockRedstoneEvent](types.md#blockredstoneevent) | A block's redstone power is changing: a lever, a button, a pressure plate, a redstone lamp or wire. Assign `event.to` to give it another power. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_redstone")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. Writable: `to`. |
| `sign_change` | [SignChangeEvent](types.md#signchangeevent) | A player finished writing on a sign. `event:cancel()` keeps the sign as it was. In this world: heard before `nf.on("sign_change")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. **Cancellable.** Bubbles. |
| `furnace_smelt` | [FurnaceSmeltEvent](types.md#furnacesmeltevent) | A furnace, smoker or blast furnace finished smelting one item. `event:cancel()` stops it: the item stays unsmelted. Assign `event.result` to make something else. In this world: heard before `nf.on("furnace_smelt")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. **Cancellable.** Bubbles. Writable: `result`. |

### Entities

| Event | Payload | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entity_spawn` | [EntitySpawnEvent](types.md#entityspawnevent) | An entity is coming into this world: before `nf.on("entity_spawn")`, with the same event, so `event:cancel()` here stops it and `event:stop()` keeps it from `nf`. **Cancellable.** Bubbles. |

### Day, night and weather

| Event | Payload | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dusk` | [DaylightEvent](types.md#daylightevent) | Night fell here: the time of day went from day (23000 to 12999) into night (13000 to 22999), by the clock or by `/time set`. Heard before `nf.on("world_dusk")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. The runtime looks at the clock every tick, and only while something listens; a jump from one night to the next (a whole day skipped) is no change, so nothing is heard. Bubbles. |
| `dawn` | [DaylightEvent](types.md#daylightevent) | Day broke here: the time of day went from night (13000 to 22999) into day (23000 to 12999), by the clock or by `/time set` (sleeping through the night too). Heard before `nf.on("world_dawn")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `weather_change` | [WeatherChangeEvent](types.md#weatherchangeevent) | It is starting or stopping raining (or snowing) in a world. `event:cancel()` keeps the weather it has. In this world: heard before `nf.on("weather_change")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. **Cancellable.** Bubbles. |
| `thunder_change` | [ThunderChangeEvent](types.md#thunderchangeevent) | A thunderstorm is starting or stopping in a world. `event:cancel()` keeps the weather it has. In this world: heard before `nf.on("thunder_change")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. **Cancellable.** Bubbles. |
| `lightning_strike` | [LightningStrikeEvent](types.md#lightningstrikeevent) | Lightning is striking: a storm, a trident with channeling, a command or a script. `event:cancel()` stops it. In this world: heard before `nf.on("lightning_strike")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. **Cancellable.** Bubbles. |

### Chunks

| Event | Payload | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chunk_load` | [ChunkLoadEvent](types.md#chunkloadevent) | A chunk came into memory: someone came near, or it was generated for the first time (`event.generated`). The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("chunk_load")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `chunk_unload` | [ChunkEvent](types.md#chunkevent) | A chunk is leaving memory, as everyone has gone away. Its blocks can still be read and changed in the handler. In this world: heard before `nf.on("chunk_unload")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `chunk_generated` | [ChunkEvent](types.md#chunkevent) | A chunk was generated, the first time it was loaded: its terrain, structures and the game's decorations are in place, so a script can add its own (a centity in a grove, a shrine on a hill). Its blocks are `event.x * 16` to `event.x * 16 + 15` across, the same along `z`, and can be read and changed in the handler; the chunks beside it may not be generated yet, so keep what you place inside it. Once per chunk, ever: one generated while no script listened isn't heard later. It happens for every new chunk a player explores, so keep handlers quick and leave most chunks alone. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("chunk_generated")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |

### `world:on(event, handler, options?)` {#on}

Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `event` | `World.Event` | The event's name. |
| `handler` | `fun(event: `[`Event`](types.md#event)`)` | Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`. |
| `options` (optional) | [`EventOptions`](types.md#eventoptions) | How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`. |

**Returns** [`Subscription`](subscription.md): Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

```lua
nf.worlds.default():on("block_place", function(event)
  event.player:send_message("Placed " .. event.state)
end)
```

### `world:once(event, handler)` {#once}

Like `world:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `event` | `World.Event` | The event's name. |
| `handler` | `fun(event: `[`Event`](types.md#event)`)` | Called with the event. |

**Returns** [`Subscription`](subscription.md): Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.
